title: GS21 with the priced y factor on the INVESTMENT COST, three exposure types (KP14's growth-option mechanism)
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when firm exposure runs through the investment option, as KP14's does through its growth options?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-09). Three GS21 constructions with y on cash flow (production, fixed cost, signed fixed cost) and one with fundamentals-driven default plus a state-dependent recovery rate all came back with the market spanning 69-92% of SR_max and a premium that is 82-87% linear in the ranks. KP14's own gap, measured on vyg30k70's panels, is a static rank-nonlinearity of the GROWTH-OPTION share within a type. GS21 has a real, lumpy investment option whose value share is 16-34% of equity across firms (optshare.py on gvy25's panels: mean 0.245, p10 0.155, p90 0.336). This spec puts the priced y factor on the INVESTMENT COST: a type-f firm's drawn cost is multiplied by exp(gs_bi y), gs_bi < 0, so investing is dear in bad states and the firm's exposure to y is proportional to the value of its live option. No level compensation: at y = 0 the types are identical.

PRE-CHECK that tempers the prediction: on gvy25's panels the option share is 79% linear in ranks of (roe, lev, size) and correlated 0.96-0.98 with leverage within a type, so within a type the exposure is close to a leverage sort; what the construction keeps is a type hidden at y = 0 (bvy25's property).

CALIBRATION (low resolution, xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 150 firms, 2026-10-09 15:30; low-res solves hit the sweep cap). gs_bi 0 / -0.5 / -1.0: type premia 3.2 / 4.9 / 5.5 %/yr, SR_max 0.20 / 0.23 / 0.32 by y-tercile, mean log size 4.13 / 4.00 / 4.34 (non-monotone: hidden). gs_bi -2.0: investment becomes so cheap in good states that the type balloons (log size 7.6, premium 8.9%) -- out. Ladder here (-0.2, -0.6, -1.0): the top at the tested value, every type loading. The premium dispersion is strongly y-dependent (cs-sd of mu 0.0008 at low y vs 0.0019 at high y), which is the state-rotation signature: read room_s against room first.

CHECKS. E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 on the calibration economies; gs_bi = 0 reproduces the solver exactly (cy = 1).

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids read from the Quest solve logs by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-09, before the run). Market share of SR_max 60-80%; room +0.01 to +0.04. The decisive read is room_s: close to room means the option channel bends the premium in the ranks and a fair gap of +0.005 to +0.012 follows; well below room means state rotation and a fair gap of about zero with linrank_s. FALSIFIED as 'the option channel ports the KP mechanism to GS21' if the fair gap is below +0.005 or positive in fewer than 7 of 10 seeds.

changes: gs_bi [-0.2, -0.6, -1.0]: each type's drawn investment cost x exp(gs_bi y); production and cost exposures 0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
